Time-resolved quantity: EEG aperiodic exponent e_i(t), estimated repeatedly from sliding spectral windows
Where ISC/synchrony is applied: Directly to the participant’s exponent trajectory versus a TD-derived exponent template
Primary question / relation to the prese: Are fluctuations of the aperiodic exponent itself temporally aligned across individuals? This is the primary naturalistic temporal readout.

Approach: Klar et al. 2025 β(t)–ISC(t) framework (main-text ref. 18)
Time-resolved quantity: fMRI scale-free spectral exponent β(t) and time-varying ISC(t) of regional BOLD activity
Where ISC/synchrony is applied: ISC(t) is computed on the regional BOLD signal; β(t) is separately estimated and then related to ISC(t)
Primary question / relation to the prese: Do time-dependent scale-free dynamics covary with the degree of shared BOLD activity? Conceptually related, but not equivalent to Aperiodic-ISC.

Approach: Conventional EEG synchrony/ISC controls in the present study
Time-resolved quantity: Broadband amplitude envelope or alpha phase-locking information
Where ISC/synchrony is applied: Signal-derived amplitude or phase coordination rather than the parameterized exponent trajectory
Primary question / relation to the prese: During Partly Cloudy, alpha PLV ISC did not differ (TD = 0.049, ASD = 0.044, p = 0.3694), whereas envelope ISC was reduced in ASD (TD = 0.305, ASD = 0.174, p = 0.0010). Aperiodic-ISC shared limited variance with envelope ISC (r2 ~ 0.037), and the group difference remained after envelope adjustment (beta = 0.052, 95% CI [0.033, 0.072], p = 1.73 × 10-7).
